title: What If You Never Slept Again?

scenes.text: What if you never slept again? Your body would not shut down first. Your mind would.
In a famous science fair project in 1965, a high school student stayed awake 264 hours, about 11 days.
Healthy people kept awake for 8 to 10 days show growing trouble with concentration, perception and judgment.
The brain starts forcing tiny microsleeps, which is why drowsy driving is so dangerous.
Those volunteers recovered after just one or two nights of sleep.
But rats kept from sleeping completely died within 11 to 32 days, linked to a runaway metabolism. Sleep is not optional.

description:
What if you never slept again?
People kept awake for 8 to 10 days lose focus and judgment, and rats kept fully awake died within weeks.
What should we run through next?
